question.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral 

$$
{∭}_{R}2xyz\,dV
$$

where the region $R$ is given by

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,0\le x\le y+z\},
$$

and $D$ is a finite region in $yz$-plane enclosed between the $y$-axis, the line $y=1$ and the line $z=y$ in the first quadrant.
question.worked_solution:
Writing down our triple integral as a mixed integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}2xyz\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{y+z}2xyz\,dx]dA.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $x,$ treating $y$ and $z$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{y+z}2xyz\,dx]dA & ={∬}_{D}yz[{x}^{2}]_{x=0}^{x=y+z}\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}yz(y+z)^{2}\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}yz({y}^{2}+2yz+{z}^{2})\,dA \\  & ={∬}_{D}{y}^{3}z+2{y}^{2}{z}^{2}+y{z}^{3}\,dA\end{aligned}
$$

We must now evaluate the double integral above over the region $D$ in the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14216491/assets/5974f852ba8dcaf9e6c4d6323709987c590e2f739524e012545738bc4bb842b0.png)

We can evaluate our double integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}{y}^{3}z+2{y}^{2}{z}^{2}+y{z}^{3}\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{y}{y}^{3}z+2{y}^{2}{z}^{2}+y{z}^{3}\,dz\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{y}{y}^{3}z+2{y}^{2}{z}^{2}+y{z}^{3}\,dz]dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{1}{2}{y}^{3}{z}^{2}+\frac{2}{3}{y}^{2}{z}^{3}+\frac{1}{4}y{z}^{4}]}_{z=0}^{z=y}dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{2}{y}^{3}\cdot {y}^{2}+\frac{2}{3}{y}^{2}\cdot {y}^{3}+\frac{1}{4}y\cdot {y}^{4}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{17}{12}{y}^{5}\,dy \\  & =\frac{17}{12}{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{5}\,dy \\  & =\frac{17}{12}{[\frac{1}{6}{y}^{6}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =\frac{17}{12}(\frac{1}{6}-0) \\  & =\frac{17}{72}\end{aligned}
$$
